title: Machine-learning-guided screening identifies Bcl-2-family inhibitors IS20 and IS21
summary: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening followed by surface-plasmon-resonance and biological assays identified IS20 and IS21 as compounds binding anti-apoptotic Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Mcl-1 proteins. Both affected cancer-cell viability and induced apoptosis/autophagic flux in tested cell models; IS21 also reduced tumor growth in leukemia and melanoma mouse models.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening (model family not named in PubMed abstract)
organization: IRCCS Regina Elena National Cancer Institute; Sapienza University of Rome; Italian National Research Council and collaborators

evidence.tested: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening followed by surface-plasmon-resonance and biological assays identified IS20 and IS21 as compounds binding anti-apoptotic Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Mcl-1 proteins.
evidence.unknown: The article calls the compounds potential/new leads; findings are biochemical, cell-based and mouse-model preclinical evidence. It does not establish clinical effectiveness. The PubMed abstract does not specify the machine-learning algorithm, so no specific model architecture is attributed here.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening prioritized putative Bcl-2-family inhibitor compounds; the candidate hits were then evaluated by surface plasmon resonance and in vitro cell assays, and IS21 was evaluated in mouse tumor models. The reported outcome is the specific assay characterization of IS20 and IS21.
